title: bug: Multipass spawns use a bare `multipass` on Windows and outside provision/runCheckJob/certify, and Windows resolves a bare name from the current directory first
description: windowsPlatform has no executable, so every win32 Multipass spawn (provision, runCheckJob, certify, doctor and cli prerequisites, vm-control, agent lifecycle) runs a bare 'multipass', which Windows libuv resolves from the cwd (.com, .exe) before PATH (Serena memory gotcha-windows-libuv-spawn-searches-cwd-first): a multipass.exe in the daemon's or CLI's cwd, e.g. an agent-written file in the project checkout, would run as the operator. On Linux and macOS, vm-control.mjs (provider = {}), the cli doctor command and agent-lifecycle.mjs also skip the platform's pinned EXECUTABLE; CQ-R13 pinned it only inside runCheckJob. Pin one absolute client on every path (verify the Windows install path on a real host), or resolve it from PATH only as source-export.mjs does for git. Until then CERTIFICATION.md has the operator run from the work dir.
definitionOfDone: No local-runner Multipass spawn on any platform runs a bare 'multipass'; a test plants multipass.exe/.com in the cwd and shows it never runs.
Each platform's client path is pinned once and used by provision, runCheckJob, certify, doctor, prerequisites, vm-control and agent lifecycle, with tests per path.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) Changing the low-level `executable = 'multipass'` defaults (multipass.mjs, lifecycle.mjs, guest-session.mjs, snapshot-transfer.mjs, check-session.mjs, certify-bridge.mjs): rejected. It adds 6 files, past the 10-file cap. Held rows assert those defaults as seams (local-runner-bridge.test.mjs:621/1645, local-runner-check.test.mjs:1058/1157, about 15 rows in local-runner.test.mjs), and check-session.mjs belongs to a80f46db next. Instead, every production entry hands over the pin. 2) Resolving the Windows client from PATH, as source-export's pathGit does for git: rejected. The v1.17.0 installer appends its bin folder to PATH LAST (Part="last"), so an earlier entry, such as the user-writable %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps, could stand in for it. That breaks the rule Linux and macOS follow (another multipass on PATH cannot stand in), and a miss would surface as PROVIDER_INPUT_INVALID, not PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND. 3) A non-enumerable windowsPlatform.executable that keeps the held rows green: rejected, because those rows assert the defect. 4) Splitting the row: rejected, because both DoD items name every path, and a split would loop back to PLANNING.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- libuv on win32 looks up a bare name in the cwd (.com, then .exe) before PATH, ignoring NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath; POSIX resolves relative or empty PATH entries against the cwd (Serena gotcha-windows-libuv-spawn-searches-cwd-first).
- canonical/multipass v1.17.0 packaging/windows/wix, read for this plan:
  - Package.wxs: Name="Multipass", INSTALLFOLDER under ProgramFiles6432Folder, BinFolder 'bin', and a WixUI_InstallDir dialog;
  - CLIClientComponents.wxs: bin\multipass.exe, with a PATH append Part="last" for the user or the system.
  The held fixtures already use 'C:\Program Files\Multipass\bin\multipass.exe'.
- provision.mjs, certify.mjs and native-smoke.mjs already use provider.executable ?? platform.executable; CQ-R13 step 3 gave check-lifecycle.mjs parse() the same pin (RX6). certify-recovery-child and check-dispatch pass platformFor(process.platform). Only windowsPlatform lacked an executable, and only the cli doctor command, vm-control and agent-lifecycle built providers with none.
- A scratch simulation of steps 2-3 against the shared tree failed exactly 7 held rows in local-runner.test.mjs: 'Windows provisioning keeps its own multipass client', CJ2, CJ9, CJ12, LC1, WC1 and AJ3. A4 and the bundle/Gradle/TY1 rows also fail in a scratch copy at baseline. The vm-control, bridge, check, snapshot and agents files stayed green.
planningNotes.risks:
- Shared checkout. CQ-R13 runs local-runner.test.mjs in place during its step 4, so any runtime edit here would turn 7 of its rows red. That is why step 1 opens with a gate on top of the governors' temporary dependsOn.
- ci.yml is also declared by 4 gated WORKING rows (0921d6d7, 3ad573a7, 4e412148, 4fdc7590). It is clean and those rows are idle, so expect a Moe-Contested trailer. It lands through an editing-tool write or a clean pre-flight.
- The tests mutate process-global state (cwd, PATH, NODE_OPTIONS, process.platform) and must restore it on every path.
- On Windows, the hard link may be refused; fall back to a copy.
- The Windows pin is checked against installer source, not a real install. CQ-R13 step 5's Windows certify run is the first check on a real host. A custom install folder fails closed with PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND, and the docs belong to CQ-R13.
- DoD 1 reading: 'spawn' means a process that a production entry starts. The low-level default parameters stay as injected-transport test seams; hardening them is a later row once the held tests free up.
